configuration: ./Config.pl -default -amrex2d -v=Empty,PC/FLEKS,GM/BATSRUS -tp=PBEG; ./Config.pl -o=GM:u=Default,e=MultiIonPe,ng=2,g=8,8,1 -o=PC:lev=9, then make SWMF and make rundir. Deck Param/PARAM.in.test.GMPC.FLEKS.2D.periodic unchanged. GM/BATSRUS sets up a doubly periodic two-ion box and hands it to PC/FLEKS, which integrates it alone; built against the true two-dimensional AMReX library (-amrex2d) and with the widest test-particle record the code offers (-tp=PBEG: position, B, E and grad-B per tracked particle). Graded: pc_z0_fluid.out.
observable: the final state of the graded window as the upstream check reads it: pc_z0_fluid.out
variant: The GM #UNIFORMSTATE mass density of the first ion fluid, multiplied by 1 + 2e-10 in ic/variant and printed to twelve significant digits -- a relative change far below any physically meaningful difference in the input and an order of magnitude above the last digit the coarsest graded ASCII file carries. It is generic numerical-noise calibration: the two inputs differ by one number, and the spread between the two runs is the floor this pass policy can be held to.
altbuild: run.sh altbuild rebuilds the same pinned source and deck with ./Config.pl -O0 (every OPTn line of Makefile.conf forced to -O0 where the shipped gfortran template builds at -O3, which is what both the Fortran rules and the C++ rule of Makefile.conf use, so the framework, BATSRUS and the FLEKS solver are all rebuilt); the floor it measures is written into evidence.floor by selfcheck.

evidence.floor_how: measured by selfcheck: run.sh altbuild against run.sh nominal, graded with this check's own validate.py

warrant: CALIBRATION RUN: the bound of this rubric is deliberately loose (|dx| <= 1e-12 + 1e-3|ref|) so that selfcheck run 1 measures the variant spread and the altbuild floor of every graded file without failing on them; the graded bounds are written from those measurements before run 2.
